items.name: SUB · Last order
items.what: Sub-workflow behind get_last_order: returns the newest order for the chat_id it is given, or found: false.
setup: Create (or reuse) a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential and select it in Orders for this chat.
Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in Orders for this chat with your sheet's ID (Orders tab with order_id, chat_id, items_json, delivery_date, created_at and the other Boss 3 columns).
Save the workflow and note its ID.
items.test: Pin {"chat_id": "512349876"} (a chat_id that has orders in your sheet) on the trigger and execute: you should get found: true with that customer's newest order. A chat_id with no orders returns found: false.

items.name: HL · Telegram agent with memory (4.3)
items.what: Telegram agent with Postgres Chat Memory keyed by tg-{chat_id} (window 8) and a get_last_order tool whose chat_id comes from the trigger.
setup: Create a free Supabase project (or use Postgres on your 3.8 server) and add a Postgres credential in n8n with the host, database, user, password and port from Supabase's Connect panel. Select it in Postgres Chat Memory.
Create a Telegram API credential with your bot token and select it in Telegram Trigger, Send reply and Send error reply.
Create an OpenAI credential and select it in Chat model. Replace YOUR_MODEL with the model you use.
In get_last_order, replace YOUR_LAST_ORDER_WORKFLOW_ID by choosing SUB · Last order from the list.
Publish (activate) the workflow; the Telegram Trigger needs your HTTPS n8n from 3.8.
items.test: From two Telegram accounts, send an address, then some items, then "where are you delivering?": each account gets only its own address. From an account with past orders, send "same as last time": the log shows a get_last_order call and the bot reads the items back and asks you to confirm.

walk.title: Build it: an agent that knows its regulars
walk.sample: Telegram chat 512349876 · "Same as last time, please" · two test accounts

steps.say: First, a free Supabase project and a Postgres credential in n8n. The password lives in the credential only, never in a node.
show: Postgres credential: host, database, user, password, port

steps.say: Messages arrive from Telegram. The chat ID on each message is who the customer really is, and we'll use it everywhere.
The agent reads the message text. Its system message says memory covers this conversation only, and that past orders come from a tool.
show: Memory: recent messages from this conversation only

steps.say: For same as last time, it must call get_last_order, read the items back and ask the customer to confirm before quoting. It never mentions other customers or repeats card numbers or PINs.
show: call get_last_order … ask them to confirm before quoting
Never ask for or repeat card numbers, PINs or passwords

steps.say: The model is the brain, as before. It decides when a message refers to an old order.
Short-term memory lives in Postgres, so it survives restarts. The session key is the chat ID, with a tg prefix so WhatsApp chats stay apart later.
Eight past interactions is enough for one order conversation and small enough to stay cheap. Not a hundred, to be safe.
Long-term memory is a tool that reads the Orders sheet through SUB Last order. Your orders are more accurate than any old chat text.
Here's the safety moment. The chat ID is mapped from the trigger, not filled by the model, so typing I'm Hotel Grace gets you nothing.
show: Takes no input from you; identified automatically

steps.say: The reply goes back to the same chat ID that sent the message, never anywhere else.
If the agent fails, its error output still sends a polite reply, so the customer isn't left waiting.
show: Sorry, something went wrong. Tolu will reply shortly.

steps.say: Test from two Telegram accounts: address, items, then where are you delivering. Each must see only their own details. Then add HL Forget old chats to delete rows older than thirty days.
show: DELETE … WHERE created_at < now() - interval '30 days'
steps.data: each account sees only its own address

walk.end: Two phones, two separate memories, and same as last time read back from the Orders sheet: the agent knows its regulars and nobody else's.

items.name: HL · Forget old chats
items.what: Daily schedule that deletes chat memory rows older than 30 days from hl_chat_memory.
setup: Select the same Postgres credential in Delete chats older than 30 days.
Open hl_chat_memory in Supabase's table editor; if there is no created_at timestamp column, add one with default now() before relying on this clean-up.
items.test: In Supabase, set one test row's created_at to 40 days ago, then click Execute workflow: that row is deleted and recent rows stay.
